scope: All device-level claims come from ONE unit, bootloader v1.0.17, unless noted. Seeds, checks and bootloader behaviour may differ on other units or bootloader versions.

statuses.observed-device: Seen on hardware; evidence pinned (photo, transcript, or recorded artifact hash plus the operator's observation).
statuses.observed-file: Verified directly against files in firmware/ (parse, CRC, diff).
statuses.deduced: Follows logically from observed-device/file results; no direct observation.
statuses.inferred-static: Derived from disassembly/static analysis only; not device-verified.
statuses.fitted: Parameter chosen to fit available samples exactly; unvalidated until a second independent sample agrees.
statuses.superseded: Shown wrong or replaced by later evidence; kept for history. The notes name the claim that replaces it.

claims.claim: Every integrity field is IEEE CRC-32 (zlib convention) over the whole image including header, with only its own checksum word zeroed, seeded by a constant per (product family, image type).
evidence: 56/56 fields across 23 releases of seven products, every field matching (tools/verified_corpus.json, checked against the files by tools/test_integrity.py)
C1 rejection of a 1-bit CRC flip
resealed CUSTOM INFO accepted and running

claims.notes: Device-level proof is specific to the SmplTrek profile; the file-level fit covers Lofi-12 XT too. The SmplTrek bootloader (BOOT 1.0.17) computes the equivalent form: zlib CRC-32 from 0 with the field replaced by a constant from code (cmtd 0xF2970822, pmtd 0xB02C53FD, mmtd 0x88E83CEB, bmtd 0xE255264C); all 22 SmplTrek images and the dump's BOOT image match (tools/test_integrity.py, docs/05-bootloader.md).

claims.claim: After OK, no writer checks the file's inner CRC before erasing: a SYSTEM image with a bad inner CRC is erased-and-written in full, fails the post-write CRC recomputation, and never gets its install marker, so normal boot refuses it (the old system is gone; bootloader and HOME + power remain). NORMAL boot does not check the installed system image's CRC: it requires only the 'mmtd' magic and bit 0 of header +12 clear (the install marker), then loads the 'sect' sections and branches to the entry point.
evidence: C2 was CLR'd at the prompt by protocol
SYSTEM DIAG does validate installed images (observed)

static, BOOT 1.0.17: BootLoader slot 1 (0xC7094E40) reads flash 0x40000 and calls no CRC routine; the CRC routine's callers are the update file check, the updater's post-write checks and SystemVerify (docs/05-bootloader.md)
claims.notes: Both halves from the BOOT 1.0.17 disassembly (2026-11-11), not device-tested; see docs/05-bootloader.md 'Writing'. Practical rule unchanged: always reseal every CRC.

claims.claim: Each SPI-flash section is written as erase -> program -> post-write CRC recomputation from flash -> program 0xFFFFFFFE over header +12 (SYSTEM 0x4000C, PRESET 0x44000C, BOOT 0x3FFF0). 'Verifying' recomputes the CRC; it does not compare with the file. BOOT, PRESET, MCU and MCU Boot sections are written only when strictly newer than the installed version (or nothing is installed); SYSTEM is always written.
evidence: BOOT 1.0.17: writers 0xC7085F74 / 0xC7085AB4 / 0xC7085E10, marker write 0xC7085A94 with the copy-table-initialised word 0xC70AD8C4 = 0xFFFFFFFE, check 0xC708D410
version compare loop 0xC7090864 (unsigned, major/minor/build)
installed images in the A4 dump carry 0xFFFFFFFE at +12 and their CRC matches with +12 restored to 0xFFFFFFFF

claims.claim: The boot area (flash 0..0x40000) is write-protected by the flash's block-protect bits; the bootloader clears them only around a BOOT section write and re-applies them (status BP=0011, configuration bit 3) after it and on every BOOT MODE entry.
evidence: BOOT 1.0.17: 0xC7095110 (status & 0xC3), 0xC70952CC (set), 0xC7095394 (check at BOOT MODE entry); flash commands 0x05, 0x15, 0x01
claims.notes: That BP=0011 + TB covers exactly 256 KiB assumes a 128 Mbit Macronix part (0x15 read-configuration convention). 2026-11-17: both devices answer 9F with C2 20 18 (Macronix, 128 Mbit) and device 0 reads BP = 0011, TB = 1 (HW-54); the exact part suffix is not known. The SYSTEM and content areas are not protected by this.

claims.claim: Apps write flash only through one shared helper pair to the top two 4 KiB sectors (0x01FFF000, 0x01FFE000): two settings blocks tagged 'PREF' and 'PREX'; tags are shared across products, layouts are not; readers validate the 4-byte tag only and rely on per-field clamps.
evidence: static reading of the app's flash writers and settings reader, 2026-11-09 (now docs/01-platform-map.md 'Flash use by the app' and 'Settings block')
same tags located in Lofi and CyDrums images
claims.notes: A foreign app would overwrite these blocks (why the C3 image was sterilised). 2026-11-10 (docs/01-platform-map.md 'Settings block', 'Flash use by the app'): holds for CyDrums 1.1.84 too. Only SmplTrek's validator reads the PREX half; Lofi-12 XT and CyDrums copy PREF (404 / 376 bytes from block+0, tag included) and reset PREX to defaults on every boot. The writer is the same structure with the same flash addresses, not byte-identical (region_diff). 2026-11-10 writer read: settings_save writes nothing unless settings_changed reports a difference from the shadow copies; per sector it erases 4 KiB, then writes each half as struct bytes 4..len-1, read-back compare, then the 4-byte tag last; the rest of each half stays 0xFF. Halves written: PREF 284 / 404 / 376 bytes, PREX 372 / 380 / 380 (SmplTrek / Lofi-12 XT / CyDrums).

claims.claim: Clocks: the oscillator input is 24 MHz, the CPU runs at 372 MHz and PLL0 SYSCLK2 (SPI0, SPI1, UART1) at 186 MHz.
evidence: SYS/BIOS programs TIMER64P0 PRD12 = 24000 for its 1 ms tick (simulated, analysis/mmio_trace.py --boot)

the SPI driver's module-clock constant 186,000,000 (0xC16716E4) gives the observed prescalers (SPIFMT0 0x10408 for 32 MHz, 0x11308 for 9 MHz); later agreement: UART0 divisor 372 = 31,250 baud exactly, MMCSD0 CLKRT 232 = 399 kHz, I2C0 prescaler for a 24 MHz input
AIS ROM function 6 arguments 0x001E0001, 2823, 3 (docs/05-bootloader.md) read as x31 / 2 from 24 MHz
claims.notes: 2026-11-12. Amended 2026-11-12 against TI documents: SPRAB41F Appendix D.1/D.7 (Arg1 = CLKMODE 0 crystal, PLLM 0x1E, PREDIV 0, POSTDIV 1; Arg2 0x000B07 = PLLDIV1 0, PLLDIV3 0x0B, PLLDIV7 7; Arg3 = SPI PRESCALE 3) and SPRUH79C Table 7-12 (multiplier = PLLM + 1, divider = RATIO + 1) give 24 x 31 / 2 = 372 MHz; SPRUH79C Table 7-1 puts UART0, SPI0, MMC/SD0 on PLL0_SYSCLK2, UART1/SPI1 on ASYNC3 (= PLL0_SYSCLK2 by default, CFGCHIP3 never written), I2C0 and Timer64P0/P1 on PLL0_AUXCLK (the 24 MHz oscillator). Cautions: the resulting PLLOUT 744 MHz is above SPRS590G Table 6-4's 300-600 MHz range; SPRS590G cites SPRAAT2, not SPRAB41, for the C6748 ROM, so the function table is assumed. docs/04-hardware-access.md.

draw_text_impl 0xC167CDC8..0xC167CDEC: odd x keeps the low nibble (mask 15) and writes grey << 4, even x keeps the high nibble (mask 0xF0 in a20)
claims.notes: 2026-11-12. Simulation with polled status registers answered 'ready'. With HW-7, answers what a first bare-metal display driver needs. docs/04-hardware-access.md. 2026-11-13, D1 run 3 on the device: wrong on the nibble order; the unit shows the high nibble as the left (even x) pixel (HW-34). The rest (SPI1, GP2[11], the four commands, 8192-byte frames) is now observed-device: the D1 test image's display works with them. 2026-11-13, D1 run 5: the nibble order is neither reading; the frame is not row-major (HW-35).

claims.claim: The panel MCU is on UART1 (PSC1 module 12, PINMUX4 nibbles 6-7 = 2) at DLL 25 / MDR 0, i.e. 465,000 baud from 186 MHz for a nominal 460,800, 8N1, FIFO trigger 1; the app sends it 0x90, 0xA0 and 0xB1 at start-up, 0xB2 at power-off, LED messages C1 a b c v and C2 x.

the one-byte senders 0xC161E4A0..0xC161E6A4 each send a constant at B14+1622..1627 (90, 91, B0, B1, B2, A0); 0xC161E72C sends C2 from B14+1628; callers read at 0xC154A804, 0xC154A8D4, 0xC154A918/944, 0xC154ADC8, 0xC15F3724

claims.claim: No watchdog runs under the stock app, and GP4[11] (power hold) is left an output by the bootloader: the app's power_on_check drives it high without setting its direction.
evidence: power_on_check 0xC1646FCC simulated: SET_DATA of bank pair 2 bit 11, no DIR write
the bootloader runs the same power_on_check before loading SYSTEM (docs/05-bootloader.md)
no timer register constant in the bootloader; the app uses TIMER64P1 only as a free-running counter (audio_clock_probe_tick) and TIMER64P0 for the tick

device, D0 2026-11-12: with a SYSTEM image that executes only a self-branch, the unit stayed on for minutes after the power key was released, so the bootloader's power_on_check latches GP4[11] before SYSTEM starts (a reset would have dropped the hold and switched the unit off)
claims.notes: 2026-11-12. The direction is inference: it follows only if the bootloader's call sets the pin before SYSTEM starts and nothing resets it (D0 2026-11-12 shows it does set the pin; the no-reset half of the claim is also consistent with D0, since a reset loop would have switched the unit off). A watchdog enabled by the boot ROM is excluded only by the C6748 reset defaults, not checked here. docs/04-hardware-access.md.

claims.claim: The codec's master clock input is 24.576 MHz: the apps program PLL on, P = 2, J = 8, D = 0 (44.1 kHz: J = 7, D = 3500), leave register 11 (R = 1) and register 102 (PLLCLK_IN = MCLK) at reset, and fs(ref) = MCLK x K x R / (2048 x P) is 48 kHz only for MCLK = 24.576 MHz. Register 7 (0x0A / 0x8A) is the datapath register (fs(ref) select, left/right DAC data), not part of the PLL.
evidence: codec_set_sample_rate 0xC161D560 simulated in the three products (analysis/codec_map.py, test_codec_map.py)

claims.claim: USB0 can carry at most one 1024-byte isochronous packet per endpoint per (micro)frame: 4 TX and 4 RX endpoints besides EP0, 4 KiB FIFO RAM (EP0 fixed at 64 bytes), MAXPAYLOAD up to 1024 with TXMAXP/RXMAXP bits 15-11 reserved (no high-bandwidth multiplier). At 48 kHz with one spare frame per packet, one endpoint per direction carries 10 (16-bit) / 6 (24-bit) channels at full speed and 73 / 48 channels at high speed. FIFO RAM fits two 1024-byte isochronous endpoints, at most one of them double-buffered, beside EP0 and the stock MIDI endpoints. The stock FIFO plan uses 960 bytes.
